phase_task.goal: The hand-written agent control loop: plan → retrieve → edit → verify → repair, bounded by step and token budgets, with a durable journal that makes runs resumable and replayable. This is the core the assignment says must NOT be hidden inside a framework — own every transition. Wire together the Phase-1 index, Phase-2 budgeted retrieval, and Phase-3 sandbox verification, driven by the Model Gateway. Single-file change is the target; multi-file and self-repair-from-real-output are Phase 5. Budget enforcement wiring lands here; the consumer HTTP API is Phase 6.

deliverables.d: Model Gateway: implement the deterministic XML stub backend (keyless, reproducible) AND the Claude backend seam behind one interface. All model I/O is strict XML with SEPARATE labeled channels: trusted instruction (from the authenticated user) vs untrusted data (retrieved code). Retrieved content is always in the data channel and can never be interpreted as a command. The API key lives only in the gateway. The stub is what the eval runs against — it must be deterministic given (journal state, inputs).

Hand-written control loop as an explicit state machine (NOT a framework): plan → retrieve → edit → verify → repair. Each transition is code you own and can single-step. The agent proposes edits as span/patch operations (the Phase-3 JSON patch envelope), not whole-file blobs where avoidable. Bounded by step budget AND token budget.

Append-only journal: every model call, tool/retrieval call, and patch is journaled with (task_id, step_index) idempotency BEFORE its effect is committed. On resume, the loop replays the journal — a completed model call returns its cached response (no re-charge), an already-applied patch is not re-applied (gated on the artifact content-hash / applied flag). State the guarantee explicitly: at-least-once execution + idempotent effects = effectively-once.

Budget enforcement, server-side, at the loop: token + step + wall-clock budgets checked BEFORE each paid operation (same reserve/commit discipline as Phase-2 retrieval). A run that hits any limit stops CLEANLY at a consistent journaled checkpoint and reports partial progress — it does not overrun and does not corrupt the workspace.

Exactly three terminal states, never a silent or fabricated success: verified-success (Phase-3 sandbox says applied+built+tests_passed), give-up-with-reason, budget-exhausted. "Verified" comes only from the sandbox result, never from a model self-report.

Progress events: the loop emits a stream of events (plan, each step, tool calls, verification result, terminal state) — the same journal that backs replay is the per-run trace. Expose via agentctl (e.g. agentctl task run / task trace) for operator inspection. Consumer SSE endpoint is Phase 6.

Per-task isolated workspace: the loop operates on an isolated view (worktree/COW/snapshot — implement open_worktree, deferred in Phase 1) so a run cannot corrupt the base or another concurrent run. Concurrent-write conflict handling can be minimal here and hardened in Phase 5, but state the approach.

phase_task.oracle: Via make test (stub model, deterministic; Docker for the verify step): (1) a single-file change task runs end to end and reaches verified-success ONLY after the Phase-3 sandbox returns applied+built+tests_passed — assert the terminal state derives from the real sandbox result, not a model claim; (2) RESUME: kill the run mid-loop (after a journaled model call, before the next), restart, and assert it resumes from the journal WITHOUT re-issuing the paid model call (cached response used) and WITHOUT re-applying an already-applied patch — assert the ledger shows no double-charge and the patch applied exactly once; (3) BUDGET: a task with a tiny token/step budget stops at a clean journaled checkpoint in budget-exhausted state, reports partial progress, and leaves the workspace uncorrupted (assert consistent state, no overrun past the limit); (4) TRUST BOUNDARY: a retrieved file whose content contains an adversarial instruction (the Phase-1 planted injection) does NOT alter the agent's actions — the instruction stays in the data channel and the plan/edits are unchanged vs the same run without the injection; (5) determinism: the same task against the same snapshot with the stub model produces the same journal (replayable); (6) terminal states are exhaustive — a task that cannot succeed ends give-up-with-reason, never a fabricated success.
phase_task.docs: DESIGN.md: the agent-loop section — the explicit state machine and why we own it (not a framework), the plan→retrieve→edit→verify→repair transitions, the journal design, and how effectively-once is achieved (at-least-once + idempotent effects). The prompt-injection trust-boundary section — the XML instruction/data channel separation and why retrieved code cannot escalate to commands (redaction from Phase 2 is the secret layer; this is the command/data layer; sandbox egress is the backstop). Finalize ADR-0002 (isolation) with the worktree mechanism now implemented. Write ADR-0004 (delivery / consistency guarantee): effectively-once, the journal + idempotency-key design, reconciliation-on-resume for a model call that returned before the crash (how the ledger is reconciled so no double-charge and no leak). State the delivery guarantee explicitly.
phase_task.stop: Do not start Phase 5 (multi-file + self-repair). Report: the state-machine transitions as implemented; the journal schema usage and the exact resume/replay algorithm (how a completed-but-uncommitted step is reconciled — the model-call-returned-before-crash case); the model-gateway XML channel separation (how instruction vs data is enforced); how budget stop reaches a clean checkpoint; the worktree isolation mechanism; and the three terminal states with how each is reached.
